name: Moikodi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry. 1978. A comparative grammar of five Yareban family languages. Ms., SIL Ukarumpa, 33 pp. SIL L&C Archives entry 31196 (Glottolog ref 48352, the only Glottolog descriptive ref).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Grammar only (verbs, non-verbs, plurals, clitics, sentences, texts incl. a Moixodi text); states it follows the Yareba sketch PL C-29 'especially pp 672-696', i.e. it starts after the phonology paragraph; scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable/phonem = 0 hits outside texts.

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry. 1992. Moikodi Organised Phonology Data. Ms., SIL-PNG Ukarumpa, 3 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42426.
sources.note: Nothing: p.2 heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' is left empty (as is 'Syllable Patterns'); phoneme inventory, example words and the text carry no stress marks. Only conventions given concern the unwritten glottal stop between vowels.

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1977. Phoneme comparisons of the Yareban family. Ms., SIL Ukarumpa, 18 pp. SIL L&C Archives entry 31250 (Glottolog ref 302898).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: No suprasegmental section and no rule for any Yareban language. p.5 (intro to word list, in a paragraph about Oiso/Maria): 'An attempt will be made, however, to mark stress.' The 140-item comparative word list pp.6-10 marks stress with acute accents in every column including Moixodi (e.g. gasíra, gebíro, awéxa, ifúru, saxára, manáxi, wáxe, fáya, ófe, ibó, iná, ówama áxaxi, owáí, ubéí, demúdai, wanaísu): predominantly penultimate, with final and initial cases -- primary data only, no statement of placement.

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1975. A short sketch of Yareba grammar. In Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of Central and South-East Papua, PL C-29:667-729. [sister language Yareba, yare1248]
sources.note: For YAREBA (not Moikodi): sec. 2.1 p.670 'Stress is phonemic but is not marked in the examples used in this paper..'; no mention of Moikodi/Doriri (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry. Unpublished Moikodi (Moixodi) field materials, SIL-PNG Ukarumpa, 1976-1992 (word lists, texts underlying the 1977/1978 mss and the 1992 OPD).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Any fuller Moikodi phonology write-up would be here; SIL online catalogue (2015 capture) lists only the 3-page OPD, so existence is uncertain.

sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1972. Yareba phonemes. Te Reo 15: 52-57.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The full phonemic statement for the sister language Yareba to which the 1977 comparison defers ('interpreted.. the same as in Yareba'); would give the family's stress analysis (phonemic stress, any default position) that the Moixodi stress-marked list can be read against. Not Moikodi itself.
